definition: Box Backup is software for backing up files to a remote server and restoring them later.
example: An administrator uses a test restoration to confirm that archived files can be recovered.
sense_note: This is the backup tool named Box Backup, not a general reference to backups in the Box cloud platform.

definition: Brand communication expresses a brand’s identity and promises through messages and interactions across channels.
example: A service organization uses the same promise and tone in its website and customer emails.

definition: Brand strategy defines the audience, positioning, and priorities that guide how an organization builds and manages its brand.
example: A company chooses to emphasize reliability rather than low price in its product and communications decisions.

definition: Branding creates and maintains a recognizable identity and a coherent set of associations for an offering or organization.
example: A nonprofit applies consistent naming, visuals, and language across materials and events.

definition: Brand positioning defines the distinctive place a brand seeks to hold in a target audience’s mind relative to alternatives.
example: A bicycle maker positions its commuter model around easy maintenance instead of racing speed.

definition: Breeze.js is a JavaScript library for managing client-side data entities, queries, caching, and tracked changes.
example: A business application edits related customer records locally before saving them to a server.

definition: Bridal consulting advises clients on wedding choices and can coordinate selected elements of planning and preparation.
example: A consultant helps a couple choose among vendors within their budget.

definition: Brightway is an open-source framework for life-cycle assessment that models resource use and environmental impacts across supply chains.
example: An analyst compares modeled emissions from two packaging systems using documented inventory datasets.

definition: Broadcast programming selects and schedules content for distribution through a television, radio, or comparable broadcast service.
example: A scheduler places a local news program before a sports broadcast while meeting timing constraints.

definition: Browzwear is a set of digital apparel tools for designing, simulating, and reviewing three-dimensional garments.
example: A designer checks how a jacket pattern drapes on a virtual fit model before ordering a sample.

definition: Brute-force search systematically checks candidate solutions without relying on a problem-specific shortcut to restrict the search.
example: A small puzzle solver tests every permitted arrangement to confirm whether one satisfies the clues.

definition: Btrieve is an indexed record-management system that lets software store and retrieve records through keys.
example: A maintainer retrieves an invoice directly using its index key in a legacy application.

definition: Budtending is customer service in regulated cannabis retail, including explaining products and following sales controls.
example: A retail worker explains label information and checks the purchaser’s eligibility under store procedures.

definition: Bug tracking systems record, prioritize, assign, and track software defects through investigation and resolution.
example: A tester files a reproducible defect and links it to the fix and verification result.

definition: Building crates and skids constructs protective or load-bearing shipping structures suited to the weight and dimensions of goods.
example: A shop assembles a supported shipping base and crate for a fragile machine.

definition: Bullet Physics is a library for simulating collisions and physical motion of objects in three-dimensional scenes.
example: A game developer uses it to make fallen crates collide and settle on a floor.

definition: Bulma is a CSS framework that supplies reusable classes for responsive layouts and interface components.
example: A developer makes a row of cards stack vertically on narrow displays.

definition: A burndown chart plots remaining planned work against time to show how completion is progressing.
example: A team spots that several tasks remain unchanged as the iteration deadline approaches.

definition: Business excellence is a management approach to improving performance through systematic assessment, feedback, and sustained improvement.
example: An organization assesses its service quality and selects process changes based on the findings.

definition: Business integration software connects applications or data sources to exchange information and coordinate processes.
example: An integration passes completed orders from an online store to a warehouse system.

definition: Business process analysis studies how work currently flows and identifies sources of delay, error, cost, or duplication.
example: An analyst maps a purchase approval process and finds where requests are entered twice.

definition: Butchering prepares meat by breaking it down, trimming it, and portioning it into usable cuts.
example: A butcher portions a larger cut to meet a store’s weight and quality specifications.

definition: Butter Knife is an Android library that generates binding code from annotations connecting views and callbacks to application code.
example: A maintainer traces how a legacy screen binds its save button to a handler.

definition: bzip2 is a lossless compression utility and format for reducing the size of files.
example: An archivist compresses a plain-text log and later recovers the original bytes.

definition: C-CURE is a physical security platform for access control and monitoring security events in buildings.
example: A facilities operator adjusts authorized access for a restricted office area.
sense_note: The name can refer to several related product generations.

definition: C3.js is a JavaScript library that builds interactive charts on top of D3.
example: A developer displays monthly sales as a line chart with hover labels.

definition: Cable splicing joins compatible electrical or fiber-optic conductors while maintaining their required insulation, protection, and signal continuity.
example: A qualified technician joins two fiber sections and checks the resulting signal loss.

definition: cAdvisor collects resource usage and performance statistics from running containers.
example: An operator compares CPU and memory usage across containers on a host.

definition: A caesarean section is a surgical procedure for delivering a baby through incisions in the abdomen and uterus.
example: A qualified care team plans a caesarean delivery when a vaginal delivery would pose unacceptable risks.

definition: Caffe is a deep-learning framework for defining, training, and running neural-network models.
example: A researcher reproduces an older image-classification experiment from its Caffe model definition.

definition: Caffe2 is a deep-learning framework designed to run neural-network training or inference workloads across different deployment environments.
example: An engineer inspects an archived mobile inference workflow built with Caffe2.
sense_note: This is a separate framework from the original Caffe.

definition: Cairngorm was an application architecture framework for structuring software written in Adobe Flex.
example: A maintainer traces how a legacy Flex app dispatches commands in response to interface events.

definition: Cakewalk is a digital audio workstation lineage for recording, arranging, editing, and mixing music.
example: A musician edits MIDI notes and balances recorded tracks in a mix.
sense_note: The label could also refer to a software publisher or historical products under that name.

definition: Probability calibration measures or adjusts whether predicted probabilities correspond to observed outcome frequencies.
example: A model evaluator checks whether events forecast at roughly 70 percent actually occur about 70 percent of the time.

definition: Call admission control protects service quality by deciding whether the network can accept a new call with its available capacity.
example: A network declines a new voice session when it would exceed the bandwidth budget.

definition: Calyx Point is mortgage loan origination software for recording applications and managing related workflow and documentation.
example: A loan processor checks the completion status of an applicant’s required documents.

definition: Camera calibration estimates how a camera projects real-world points into images, including parameters such as focal length and lens distortion.
example: A vision engineer uses images of known reference points to estimate distortion before measuring parts.

definition: CANape is Vector software for measuring and calibrating the behavior of electronic control units.
example: A validation engineer logs controller readings and compares them with reference measurements.

definition: CanCan was a Ruby on Rails authorization library for defining what actions users may perform on application resources.
example: A developer allows ordinary users to read records but reserves editing for authorized staff.
sense_note: The later maintained fork is CanCanCan; do not assume the label refers to that fork.

definition: Candidate sourcing identifies and engages people who may be suitable for an open or anticipated role.
example: A recruiter builds a shortlist of potential candidates using the role’s required skills and experience.
